analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a tiny (INR 52 Cr mcap) immigration consultancy with anemic 0.21% ROE — this fails virtually every Fisher test for an exceptional growth company. There is no evidence of R&D, proprietary innovation, scalable sales organization, or management depth that would justify a long-term compounding thesis.
key_strengths: High promoter skin-in-the-game at 72.44% suggests aligned ownership
Optically cheap P/E of 5.25x implies low downside if earnings stabilize
Operates in a structurally growing Indian outbound migration/education services TAM
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% is effectively zero — the business is not earning its cost of capital
Micro-cap (INR 52 Cr) service firm with no moat, no IP, and commoditized competition
Zero FII interest (0.00%) and minimal DII (3.37%) signal lack of institutional conviction
red_flags: 0.21% ROE is inconsistent with a sub-6x P/E — suggests either earnings quality issues or a one-off base
No disclosed R&D or innovation pipeline (service-heavy, people-dependent model)
No visibility on management depth, customer concentration, or repeat-revenue dynamics
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my growth-investing lens, this company fails the very first of my 15 points: there is no evidence of products with sufficient market potential to drive years of 20%+ sales growth. Immigration consultancy is a fee-for-service, reputation-driven business with low switching costs, no proprietary technology, and direct exposure to regulatory shocks in destination countries (Canada, UK, Australia caps). A 0.21% ROE means the company is barely earning anything on shareholder capital — the Fisher checklist demands expanding margins and superior returns, and this is the opposite.

The 5.25x P/E looks superficially attractive to a Graham-style bargain hunter, but I buy great companies, not cheap ones. At INR 52 Cr market cap with no institutional sponsorship, no disclosed R&D spend, and no visible scuttlebutt-worthy differentiation (sales org, executive bench, labor relations), there is nothing here to concentrate capital into. I would pass and deploy capital into businesses with genuine innovation moats and 20%+ compounding potential.
